jobs.title: Data Engineer
jobs.description:
**Data Engineer**

London (Waterloo) · Full-time · Hybrid, three days per week in the office

# **Who we are**

At GetGround, our mission is to make property investment safer, faster and more accessible for everyone.

We’ve built an all-in-one property investment platform that supports investors from opportunity analysis and company formation through to financing, accounting and portfolio management. By bringing software, data and specialist services into one experience, we make property investing simpler, clearer and more cost-effective.

We’re now building the intelligence layer that will help investors understand opportunities, make better decisions and manage their portfolios. We bring together detailed knowledge of our customers’ investments, services such as mortgages, lettings and insurance, and a team that lives and breathes property.

We’re turning our property expertise into an intelligence layer that can scale. That starts with a data platform: selecting trusted sources, keeping information current and making it useful to our products and AI agents.

We’re looking for someone to own that foundation.

# **The opportunity**

You’ll define and build the data platform that powers GetGround’s intelligence layer. This is a hands-on role with substantial architectural ownership: choosing how we ingest, structure, curate and serve data, while improving the foundations we already have.

The scope goes beyond integrating with APIs. You’ll build ways to ingest unstructured policy updates, regulatory guidance and published documents, turning them into reliable data our intelligence layer can use.

You’ll work closely with engineering, product and our property experts to turn domain knowledge into useful data. You’ll also design for international expansion, so entering each new market builds on a shared platform.

There’s an opportunity to influence how we build our data organisation over time, including the capabilities, standards and future hires we need.

# **What you’ll do**

* **Own data as a product.** Start with the decisions our customers and AI agents need to make, then work backwards to the data required. Judge success by the usefulness and reliability of what you enable.
* **Be opinionated about sources and quality.** Work with our property experts to identify the most valuable datasets and assess their authority, coverage, freshness and limitations. Establish clear standards for what enters the platform and how conflicting information is handled.
* **Build ingestion beyond APIs.** Develop reliable pipelines for structured datasets, external APIs, documents and published guidance. Ingest updates from sources such as HMRC and other relevant authorities, detecting changes promptly and turning them into usable, traceable data.
* **Make data usable by our intelligence layer.** Structure and serve information so our products and AI agents can retrieve the right facts in context. Preserve source provenance, geographic scope and effective dates so consumers can distinguish current information from historical or superseded guidance.
* **Design for international expansion.** Build shared models and ingestion patterns that accommodate differences in property markets, tax systems and regulation. When we expand geographies, we want to go at speed, without rebuilding the platform.
* **Own reliability throughout the lifecycle.** Build monitoring, validation and recovery into ingestion, transformation, storage and serving. Know what is stale, missing or incorrect, understand the customer impact and address the root cause.
* **Set the technical direction and deliver it.** Make clear trade-offs between immediate product needs and long-term architecture. Ship useful improvements early, document decisions and help shape the standards and future team needed to support the platform.

# **What you bring**

* **Experience owning substantial data systems.** You’ve designed, built and operated production data platforms or major parts of them, and can explain the architectural decisions you made and their consequences.
* **Strong engineering fundamentals**. You bring strong SQL, data modelling and production programming skills, with practical experience in orchestration, testing, deployment and operating reliable pipelines.
* **Judgment about the data itself.** You can evaluate whether a source is fit for a particular use, reconcile inconsistent information and make uncertainty or gaps visible to downstream consumers.
* **Experience with messy external sources.** You’ve handled inconsistent formats, changing schemas, incomplete records, rate limits and integration failures. You’re comfortable working beyond clean, well-documented APIs.
* **A product mindset.** You care about the decisions your data supports. You can work with domain experts and product engineers to translate an ambiguous need into a useful data product.
* **Architectural ownership.** You can review an existing system, establish a direction and deliver improvements incrementally. You understand access controls, privacy and the responsibilities that come with combining customer and external data.
* **Clear communication and initiative**. You surface problems early, write down decisions and challenge assumptions constructively. You’re comfortable making progress without a fully specified ticket.

## **Bonus**

* Experience building data foundations for AI products, including retrieval, document processing or evaluating the quality of information supplied to agents.
* Experience modelling policy or regulatory information, including versioning and effective dates.
* Experience with property, financial services, geospatial data or international datasets.
* Familiarity with GCP, where we run our infrastructure, and experience working alongside backend engineering teams.
* Experience establishing data standards or helping build a data team.

# **This role isn’t for you if**

* **You just want to keep the pipelines running.** You’ll need to care about which data we use, whether it can be trusted and how it improves the decisions our products support.
* **You want a fully specified architecture to implement.** We need someone who can assess what exists, challenge assumptions and take ownership of the technical direction.
* **You only want to work with clean, structured data**. Important information arrives through documents, policy announcements and inconsistent external sources. Making it usable is part of the job.
* **You want to stay removed from the product or domain.** You’ll work closely with product engineers and property experts. Understanding what the data means and how it is used is essential.
* **You don’t connect with how we work.** Our values—No BS, pursuit of excellence, feedback obsessed and healthy ego—mean communicating directly, holding a high bar, seeking feedback and being willing to change your mind.

# **Why join**

* Own a data platform central to GetGround’s next phase of product development.
* Turn deep property expertise into intelligence that helps real investors.
* Work on challenging problems across customer data, property information, AI and regulated services.
* Shape the architecture for international expansion and help build our future data organisation.
* Competitive salary and meaningful equity.
* Hybrid London working, with three days per week in Waterloo.
* Benefits include private health and dental cover, a learning budget, a home-office setup budget and 12 mental health days per year.

This is a high impact, visible role. As our Founder Associate, you'll support the CEO & COO and augment their capacity by taking on problems to solve that are critically important to how we build all aspects of GetGround. Some weeks that means building the model that decides whether we enter a new market. Others it means untangling why a core funnel is leaking, or writing the board paper, or problem solving what seems like the impossible task. You'll be in a role that will require you to use your expert communication skills, analytical mindset, commercial accumen and intellect to support in propelling us through our next stage of growth.

**What you'll do**

* **Own the CEO & COO’s highest-priority problems end to end**, usually two or three at a time, each lasting anywhere from a fortnight to a quarter. You'll define the question, do the analysis, form a view, get buy-in, and see it through to execution.
* **Do the analysis yourself.** You'll pull the data, build the model, and stress-test your own conclusions before anyone else does. We don't have an army of analysts for you to delegate to, and we like it that way.
* **Turn strategy into things that ship.** You will be accountable for shipping these initiatives, creating impact and own the result.
* **Prepare the CEO & COO for the rooms that matter**, board meetings, investor conversations, partnership negotiations. You'll shape what gets said.

* Agency and resilience
* A unwavering work ethic and desire to scale a business
* 2 to 5 + years in strategy consulting, investment banking, private equity, or an operating role at a high-growth startup.

**Sales Operations Manager** (Maternity leave cover), based in central Manchester.

Note - this role requires you to be in the office 3 days per week, with 2 days work from home.

We source, structure and launch off-plan developments with developer partners, then sell them to a direct investor base and agent network. The commercial side of that is well covered. The legal and due diligence side currently sits with two senior people alongside everything else, which means partner vetting and contract review compete for time with deal-making.

This role owns that work end to end. You will prove a development partner is who they say they are and can deliver, get the contractual position right before we go to market, and stay with the scheme through launch, exchange and completion. You will also sit between Development, Progression, Sales and Marketing, making sure what we have signed and what we are selling match.

What you will do

**Partner due diligence**

* Verify the development team (developer, architect, contractor)
* Check proof of land ownership, planning permission, proof of funder and deposit protection
* Confirm the freeholder and any differentiating SPV details
* Investigate SPV directors for adverse reports or ongoing legal proceedings
* Review financial statements and assess whether a partner can actually deliver
* Run AML checks on all development partners

**Development due diligence**

* Lease details, construction schedule, short stop and long stop dates
* Build and construction warranty documentation
* Service charge estimates, confirmation of no ground rent, penalties for late completion
* How and where funds are held, with minimum 10% deposit protection
* How the land was purchased, and whether any third party holds a charge over it
* Cross-reference the scheme against current legislation, including space standards

**Legal and contracts**

* Review draft contracts and leases
* Legal onboarding of new development partners
* Internal agency and development agreements
* Panel solicitors and enquiries, onboarding client solicitors with Progression and flagging issues early

**Pre-development**

* Meeting prep and DD ahead of developer meetings, including market research on the location and their stock
* Preparatory work on pricing and the exit plan for a new partner
* Attend first developer and partner meetings in person
* Make sure notes are taken and follow-ups tracked

**Launch and ongoing**

* Contribute to client-facing assets (CGIs, brochures, floorplans) and check claims are contractually supportable
* Support tender documents: sales velocity, sales proposals, marketing proposals
* Coordinate with Marketing, Growth and Sales on launch activity and campaign feedback
* Produce developer account management documents and quarterly developer and marketing reports
* Coordinate and attend after-sales meetings with developers
* Track exchange and conveyancing: average deal length, developer satisfaction, progression blockers
* Chase developers on overdue invoices

**Completion**

* Pre-completion prep with Progression, 3 to 6 months out
* Confirm when valuations begin with Progression and the developer
* Prepare valuation documents and reports for valuers
* Hand over to Completions as mortgage and client management begins

What we are looking for

**Essential**

* A mix of sales and legal experience in UK residential property, development or construction, or equivalent hands-on DD and contract review experience
* Practical understanding of off-plan sales: reservation agreements, deposit protection, exchange, long stop dates, and what goes wrong between exchange and completion
* Able to read a lease, a build contract and a set of accounts and form a clear view on risk
* Comfortable running AML and company director checks, and knowing when to escalate
* Clear written work that a commercial audience will read and act on
* Genuinely cross-functional, and comfortable holding a line with a sales team that wants to launch on Friday
* Organised enough to own document control across multiple live schemes without being chased

We're looking for a **Compliance and Risk Lead** to be the hands-on engine of GetGround's compliance function, owning the day-to-day delivery of our regulatory obligations and helping build the frameworks that keep us operating with integrity as we scale.

## The Opportunity

GetGround operates at the intersection of fintech, proptech and wealthtech, a business with a complex and growing regulatory footprint. With £2Bn+ in assets on platform and 30,000+ users across 70 countries, our compliance obligations are significant and expanding.

This is a role with real ownership and some people management responsibility. You'll be doing the work and leading a small team to help deliver it. You'll be the person who makes compliance and risk happen at GetGround.

## What You'll Be Doing

### Day-to-Day Compliance

* Own the delivery of GetGround's compliance monitoring programme, including reviews, testing, and reporting
* Develop and manage a high-performing compliance and risk team as GetGround scales
* Maintain and update compliance policies, procedures, and controls as regulations evolve
* Support the management of regulatory relationships, including FCA interactions and reporting
* Track regulatory developments and translate them into clear, actionable guidance for the business
* Assist with the preparation of board and senior leadership compliance reporting

### Risk

* Support the identification, assessment, and monitoring of operational and regulatory risks across the business
* Maintain the risk register and assist with preparing risk reporting for senior leadership
* Work with teams across the business to ensure risk considerations are embedded into day-to-day decisions
* Help develop and maintain risk policies and frameworks as the business grows

### Financial Crime and AML

* Support the MLRO with day-to-day AML and financial crime operations, including transaction monitoring and sanctions screening
* Conduct and review KYC processes, escalating complex cases as appropriate
* Assist with SAR filing processes and maintain accurate financial crime records
* Help ensure GetGround's financial crime controls remain fit for purpose as the business grows

### Business Partnership

* Work with Product and Engineering teams to review new features and products for compliance implications
* Support the review of customer-facing content, marketing materials, and regulated communications

This is a hands-on, fully remote role in one of Plentific's cross-functional product engineering teams. The Senior Backend Engineer works alongside product managers, frontend engineers, quality engineers, and other backend engineers to build and operate the services behind repairs, quoting and invoicing, payments, contractor search, messaging, notifications, and fraud prevention. The role is open across the European countries where we currently employ or engage remote engineers.

Our backend is built primarily in Python and Django, with Django REST Framework and FastAPI supporting APIs in a service-oriented architecture deployed on AWS and Kubernetes. PostgreSQL, Redis, and Celery underpin data-intensive and asynchronous workflows. The systems handle complex permissions, legacy integrations, high transaction volumes, and business processes where reliability and data correctness matter.

AI-assisted, spec-driven development is part of normal engineering practice at Plentific. The Senior Backend Engineer turns product requirements into implementation-ready specifications, uses agentic coding tools across implementation, testing, review, and documentation, and remains accountable for the resulting software. AI-generated output is held to the same standard as human-written code. Success means delivering reliable services, improving the codebase and engineering practice around the role, and enabling the wider team to ship confidently at pace.

* Build and maintain APIs, microservices, and data pipelines using Python, Django, Django REST Framework, FastAPI, and related platform tooling.

* Develop asynchronous and event-driven workflows using technologies such as Celery and Redis.
* Write complex SQL, evolve PostgreSQL schemas safely, and optimise database performance where customer experience or operational throughput depends on it.
* Review, refactor, and retire existing code so it remains readable, testable, maintainable, and suitable for new product requirements.

jobs.description:
# About Nous

**Nous is an AI agent** that takes some of the load of life; making good decisions and acting for our users in areas where they’re not the experts or aren’t paying enough attention. We've started with optimising bills, where we're already saving households thousands, and are now expanding into new categories. Similar to how Amazon picked books as its first category and grew from there.

**We’re growing fast, and it's working.** 20x YoY growth makes us one of the fastest scaling startups in the UK. And NPS of +70 (higher than Apple) shows that our users love it.

We've just launched two more novel new products (on top of our existing bill optimisation). Insurance: we're the first to get the regulatory approval and build the tech to actually do the full insurance discovery and purchase journey as an agent for the user (not just give them a link to the best deal). Subscription management: lots of companies use Open Banking to draw pretty graphs – we're the first to use it to actively save people money starting by cancelling unwanted subscriptions for them.

It would be easy to look at this and think we've got it all figured out. But we've only scratched the surface; our ambitions are SO much higher.

**We’re building a new category of product** which is hard, so we’ve stacked the deck in our favour: an experienced founding team with multiple exits, and investors including the founders of Monzo, Wise, [Booking.com](http://Booking.com), [lastminute.com](http://lastminute.com), Onfido, Funding Circle, Tide, Habito and more.

Still - **the problems we’re solving are hard**. *‘Talk is cheap’* applies to agents too. To have REAL impact, agents need to break out of the sandbox and take action in the real world where there are consequences. This means solving all the hard, thorny, interesting, frustrating problems the real world has to offer.

## ABOUT THE ROLE

**Nous is one of the UK’s fastest-growing, AI-native consumer start-ups. We’re looking for a commercially minded Growth Lead to help us continue to scale.**

We're hiring now because a member of the team is going on maternity leave, but this isn't fixed-term cover. You'll start on influencer — our biggest acquisition channel — and we'll expect you to be leading a second growth area within your first year. When they return, the team will be bigger and so your remit will grow. Nous is scaling *very* fast, and what that second area is will depend on where the business needs you most by then.

We don’t expect you to have spent years in influencer marketing. You might come from B2B sales, partnerships, or another growth role where you’ve built a strong understanding of relationship management and what makes audiences take action. What matters is that you can apply that knowledge quickly.

Your goal will be performance, not brand or reach. You’ll be hands-on across the channel: finding creators, negotiating fees, writing briefs, reviewing content and managing campaigns. You’ll also help answer the bigger questions — who should we work with, what should we pay, what content converts, and how do we scale the channel profitably?

We’ve built internal tools to manage everything from creator outreach to performance and payments, and we’re constantly improving them. You don’t need to be an engineer, but you do need to be toolsy – using AI to automate repetitive work, improve processes and build better ways of working.

## WHAT YOU’LL DO

* **Run influencer campaigns end-to-end** — finding creators, outreach, negotiation, briefing, approvals and performance review.
* **Make commercial decisions** — work out what creators are worth, negotiate fees and structure deals that make sense for us.
* **Create content that converts** — write strong briefs and give clear feedback on creator content.
* **Own performance** — understand how we’re tracking against volume and CAC targets and act when we’re falling behind.
* **Grow the channel** — test new creators, propositions, platforms and approaches, then scale what works.
* **Make us more efficient** — use AI, internal tools and better processes to reduce manual work as the channel grows.

## ABOUT YOU

We’re open-minded about exactly where you’ve come from. You might come from B2B sales, affiliates, partnerships or another performance-focused growth role.

Across energy, mobile, broadband, insurance and subscriptions, Nous has grown 20x in the last 12 months. Our reporting hasn't always kept pace. We're hiring a Head of Business Intelligence to own this and fix it.

That means you'll set the standards rather than inherit them. No legacy team, no committee, no five-year-old semantic layer you're not allowed to touch. Which cuts both ways.

Take our unit economics. Revenue per household is a commercial assumption rather than a column in a table, and it varies as a function of behaviour, service lines managed, engagement. Some users are Premium, some not; some suppliers pay a bounty per switch, some pay nothing. Households change providers, cancel services, then switch again, and their value compounds over time in a complex way. Getting from a decent estimate to a genuinely defensible view of LTV, payback and cohort behaviour is one of the highest-leverage things anyone could do here, and it's the kind of problem that has no textbook answer.

To get there you'll own the data foundations too: canonical definitions of our fundamental metrics, the dbt models underneath them, and the reporting that Growth, Commercial, Operations and Finance depend on. We've built quickly and there's real judgment and craft required to make that as solid as the business now requires but doing so in a scrappy and pragmatic way.

You'd work directly with the senior team: CEO, Head of Finance, and the Growth, Commercial, Operations and Product leads. Your work is what the board sees. jobs.description:
## **About Nous**

Nous is an AI agent that takes some of the load of life: making good decisions and acting for people in areas where they're not the experts, or aren't paying enough attention. We started with bills, where we're already saving households thousands, and we're now expanding into new categories. Think Amazon starting with books.

It's working. 20x year-on-year growth makes us one of the fastest-scaling startups in the UK, and an NPS of +70 (higher than Apple) says our users love it. On top of bill optimisation, we've just launched two more products: insurance, where we're the first in the UK to get regulatory approval to run the full discovery-and-purchase journey as an agent (not just hand you a link). And subscription management, where we use Open Banking to actively cancel unwanted subscriptions for people, rather than just draw them a pretty graph.

We're a certified B Corp, and that's how we hold ourselves to the mission rather than just talking about it. We've stacked the deck: a founding team with multiple exits, and investors including the founders of Monzo, Wise, Booking.com, lastminute.com, Onfido, Funding Circle, Tide and Habito.

The problems are hard, and that's the point. Talk is cheap, and that goes for agents too. To have real impact, an agent has to break out of the sandbox and act in the real world, where there are consequences. That means solving all the thorny, frustrating, genuinely interesting problems the real world throws up.

## **How we build (worth reading before the role)**

Most companies split the thinkers, the doers and the builders. We don't. Something special happens when they're the same people: a small team that builds and owns the tools for its own problems understands those problems from the inside. So the rule at Nous is simple. The person who feels the problem should be the one who builds the fix.

This isn't brand new. A sharp generalist could always wire something together with no-code and low-code tools to solve a problem. The catch was the ceiling: those tools were far more limited than real code, so you hit a wall the moment the problem got interesting. Unless you had superhuman levels of stubbornness and a high tolerance for using tools for things they really weren't designed for. What's changed is that ceiling. With AI tooling and a lot of context, you're now building much closer to real code, and shipping it on the live product. You can change how our WhatsApp agent handles a tricky conversation, dig through Open Banking data to find money we should be saving people, prototype a feature, or automate a process that used to eat someone's week.

And you're not doing this around engineering, you're doing it alongside engineers. Engineers build the safe surfaces you ship on (the tools, the infrastructure, the context APIs, the guardrails), and they're who you pull in when you reach the edge of what's safe to touch alone.

None of that works without a particular kind of person: not a software engineer, but someone who builds like one.

## **The role**

You'll own a product surface and make it better, end to end, without waiting for an engineer to do it for you.

The clearest version of this already exists on the team. Ben joined as a PM, not an engineer. Engineering set him up with the right infrastructure and a context API, and now he ships changes to Nora (our customer-facing WhatsApp agent) himself, pulling people in only when he's blocked.

Worth being upfront: we've never hired for this profile directly before. The people doing it today grew into it here (Ben from product, Gen from ops) once we set them up with the tooling and context to build. You'd be the first we bring in, so expect the role to shift a bit as we figure out what works.

Depending on where you're strongest and where we need you most, the first surface might be:

* **Nora and our AI agents.** Find where she struggles in real conversations, improve how she handles them, build and run the evals that tell us whether she's getting better, and tighten the recovery flows for when things go wrong.
* **Open Banking and subscriptions.** Dig into the data behind our subscription product, spot the patterns, and build the logic that decides what's worth cancelling or flagging. Then work out how we cancel them automatically. Real money back in people's pockets.
* **Whatever's most broken.** New products and surfaces appear constantly. You'll take a rough, messy problem and turn it into something shipped and improving.

## **What you'll actually do**

* Take a product problem from rough to shipped, with AI tooling (Claude Code, Cursor, whatever gets it done) as your main working environment.
* Answer your own questions. When you need to know how many members hit a broken flow last week, write the query and find out. Don't file a ticket and wait.
* Ship on the safe surfaces: prompts, agent behaviour, configuration, workflows, data pipelines, internal tools. Know where the edge is, and pull in an engineer before you cross it.
* Live close to the user. Read the conversations, watch where the product delights people or falls over, and let that drive what you build next.
* Own the outcome. A feature isn't done when you've shipped it, it's done when it's working for members.

## **About you**

You build without precise instructions. You've been a founder, an early PM, or the generalist who ends up owning the thing nobody else will. Give you a problem and some context and you start building. You don't wait for a spec or a map.

AI tooling is already how you work. Not "ChatGPT wrote my cover letter". You use Claude Code, Cursor or similar as your working environment: prototyping, querying data, navigating systems, automating your own work. You've felt the shift where one person with the right tools does in an afternoon what used to take a sprint, and you've leaned into it. You're getting a sense of what problems are now much easier, and which aren't.

You're not a software engineer, and you don't need to be. You're technically fearless yet humble about your limitations. You'll happily get under the bonnet, read enough code to be dangerous, write a bit of SQL, and pick up a new tool before anyone hands it to you. And you have good judgement on when you should ask for help.

You've got product judgement. You can tell a real problem from a shiny one, you frame things around what changes for the member, and you kill your own ideas as readily as you back them.

You've been at this a while. You've done the doing long enough to have the scars, and you've owned something real before. This isn't a first job, and you'll be trusted to own a surface early.

Nice-to-haves:

* You've built and shipped your own thing: a startup, a side project, an internal tool that took off.
* You've worked with LLMs, agents or evals, or with messy real-world data (Open Banking, financial, operational).
* Startup experience where you wore several hats and none of them fit.

## **How we work**

We keep the middle thin, on purpose. There's barely any middle management, which means fewer bottlenecks and room for exceptional people to have real impact without first being promoted into managing others. It's a real bet, not a free lunch. Instead of a manager buffer, you get lots of context and colleagues who help because they're invested, not because an org chart says so. If you need a clear remit handed down before you can move, this probably won't suit you.

Your first 90 days are built around getting you to real ownership safely: pairing when you want it, lots of context, and people who want you to ship. We celebrate the person who built the unglamorous version this week, not whoever thought of it first.

We're office-first, near Farringdon. We do a lot of our best thinking together and being in the same room helps, though we're pragmatic about heads-down work when you need it.

## **Remuneration and benefits**

Compelling package including share options with life-changing ups...

* **Industry high-performers.** High-calibre candidates already in industry who want a controller-track role in a rapidly growing company.

```
👋 Hi, I’m Sina, CTO at Nous. 

I’ve spent my entire career in startups, starting my first company when I was a teenager, and navigated many 0→1 journeys (including starting the largest social network of its time in my home country).

The common thread that led me here is finding complexity that wastes people’s time or money, then solving for making them disappear. And that’s exactly what Nous aims to do.

If this problem space resonates, please read on. 

PS: I’ve actually written this page with my hands; this is not AI-written content!
```

# About Nous

Roughly **90% of UK households are overpaying** on their bills. Nous is an agent to absorb complexity out of households, saving them money and time. Our mission is to make people’s lives simpler and fairer, starting with the 30 million households here in the UK, and soon far beyond.

Nous is growing fast, and it’s working. 20x YoY growth makes us one of the fastest scaling startups in the UK. And NPS of +70 (higher than Apple) shows that our users love it.

We’ve just launched two novel new products (on top of our current service lines). Insurance: we’re the first to get the regulatory approval and build the tech to actually do the full insurance discovery and purchase journey as an agent for the user (not just give them a link to the best deal). Subscription management: lots of companies use open banking to draw pretty graphs - we’re the first to use it to actively save people money starting by cancelling unwanted subscriptions for them.

It would be easy to look at this and think we’ve got it all figured out.

But we’ve only scratched the surface; our ambitions are SO much higher. We started with bills because ‘change begins at home’ - it’s a naturally low-interest, messy area of our lives which most of us don’t want to think about. Similar to how Amazon started with books as their first category to go after.

*‘Talk is cheap. Action is what really matters’.* What we’re building is an agent to take some of the load of life, make good decisions and act for us in areas we can’t or don’t want to act on our own. For an agent, advice is cheap. Action is the product. And **action means solving problems in the messy real world**.

## A note on product

There’s ‘product’ as in the web application that guides our users through the complex world of bills and household admin. It acts as their interface to our management service, as well as all the behind the scenes capabilities needed to orchestrate and deliver that service - actually saving our users money and time. Try it here: [app.nous.co/signup](http://app.nous.co/signup) (it’s free!)

Then there’s ‘product’ as experienced by our users - which is a service which makes life simple and fair. To deliver this we’ve built a set of powerful capabilities that let us run and improve the service efficiently at scale: agentic communication, multimodal data extraction, orchestration for long-running operational processes, recommendations, our own agentic harness, and more. We compose these into executable workflows that deliver real outcomes for members, like switching someone to a better energy deal without the hassle.

Today, we help manage six areas of household spending: Energy, Mobile, Broadband, Mortgage, Personal finances (e.g., managing subscriptions), and Insurance. But we’re just getting started. Behind the scenes, we’ve built the technology (we call it Blueprints) that acts as rails for us to quickly expand on the breadth and depth of our service lines.

# The role

We need your help building a world-class product that will be used regularly by millions of people; which means figuring out, together, what it really takes to absorb household complexity.

As a product engineer, we'll empower you with context to enable fast iterations, end-to-end ownership and lots of agency. You’ll be a hands-on technical leader on some of the highest-leverage areas of our codebase, from building out agentic capabilities to scaling our service logic.

Some examples of the types of problems you'll solve:

* **Anton** led and shipped an entire product line around open banking and subscription management three months after joining. Yes, he had support from legal, design, commercial and his team (we even became FCA registered). But one product engineer still took it from idea to a best-in-class product in the category.
* **Ed** led the our latest Blueprint architecture, which now powers every service line. Changes to complex, long-running workflows that once took weeks can now sometimes take minutes. All safely, reliably and with full type safety.
* **Tim** led and shipped our car insurance product line, in less than 3 months. We built a journey where an agent performs the discovery and purchase journeys - something that's not been done before and needed problem solving at the intersection of engineering, product and regulatory.
* As a team, we built our own agentic harness (we call it super-engineer); it’s enabled us to build faster, investigate complex cross-system issues effectively; and it self-improves.

There are also so many [interesting problems](https://www.nous.co/careers) we are in the infancy of solving. Just as an example - user’s trust us with their Open Banking data - but it’s just lists of transactions. How can we use that stream of information and combine it with all the other data we have, to reduce friction from their lives?

Every week, we’re building tools for ourselves and evolving how we work, to make ourselves more effective. I strongly believe in the value of compounding gains, and much of our focus goes into investing in what results in exponential growth.

Although our stack is constantly evolving (and you can help shape that), here’s a current snapshot:

* Full-stack TypeScript, React, Postgres, and Temporal for long-running orchestration.
* Infra: AWS, Terraform, strong observability via Sentry and Datadog (full-stack, not just logs).
* Data: we lean heavily on Snowflake, Omni, dbt, Fivetran, Amplitude and Segment — and we’ve even built some of our own tooling to understand how well we’re helping our members.
* And we use Github, Linear, Graphite, and Blacksmith every day. We choose the best tool for the job, and don’t obsess around specific technologies.
* We also heavily rely on our wide range of agentic and tooling harness that we build and iterate on across the team. They’re part of the “secret” behind how we move fast, reliably.

You’ll report directly to the CTO (and we’ll work closely), so will be in the room for key architectural and product decisions. We’re deliberately light on layers of management: exceptional individual contributors shape direction by solving hard problems.

We organise around small product squads (around 5–7 people) with a single shared objective; and ship and learn fast.

Industrial labor is one of the most acute bottlenecks in the global economy. Operators are expensive, hard to retain, and working in environments that are increasingly unsafe. The shortage is structural. The window to solve it is now.

Already live across multiple sites and customers in Europe - spanning logistics and warehousing, industrial manufacturing, and large-scale chemical production - with a US expansion underway.

The mission is to make productivity limitless. Come and help us build it.

**The Role**

A European building materials group has agreed with Hive at CEO level to roll out supervised autonomy across its quarries. Pilots are running, and the agreement covers around 80 sites in several countries over the next years.

The signed agreement is where your work starts. Head office has said yes, but every site still has to: the plant manager, the safety team and the production planner. You get each site commercially ready before our Delivery team arrives, and you decide with the customer in which order sites go live.

This role sits between Sales and Delivery. Account Executives land new customers. Delivery installs and runs the machines. You own the rollout inside the accounts that have already signed at group level, starting with this one and followed by the next global customers.

Nobody has held this job at Hive before. How you run this account becomes how Hive runs every global account after it.

**What You Will Do**

**Own the rollout plan**

* Build the site by site rollout plan with the customer's executive sponsor.
* Sequence the rollout against what Hive can actually deliver, and defend that sequence to the customer and internally.
* Get each site to yes on its own numbers.

**Build the business case per site**

* Set the commercial terms per site inside the frame agreement: KPI thresholds, scaling estimates, exit criteria and pricing.
* Find the value beyond labour cost, such as pit design, shift patterns and production planning, and build the case the plant director takes to their board.

**Run the relationship**

* Keep the stakeholder map current in every country, from the group executive sponsor to the site supervisor.
* Run the governance: monthly with the customer's programme owner, quarterly with their executive sponsor, weekly with Hive's Delivery lead.
* Hand each site over to Delivery once it is scoped, then move to the next.

**Build the model**

* Carry customer requests into Product and Engineering, and push back on the ones that are not worth building.
* Document how Hive runs a global account, and hand it to the person who takes the next one.

**What We're Looking For**

**Essential**

* You have run a multi-site or multi-country programme, either on the vendor side or as the customer's programme owner.
* You have owned a number on an account: revenue, margin or a rollout target.
* Experience building business cases and working with both executive teams and site operations.
* Industrial context: construction, quarrying, mining, building materials, infrastructure or process industry.
* Highly structured, and comfortable owning the details over a long programme.
* You have told a customer no on scope, price or date, and kept the relationship.
* A life situation that allows heavy travel in the UK and Europe.
* Right to work in the UK.

**Strongly Preferred**

* Operations or strategy consulting experience with industrial or infrastructure clients.
* Experience from a large construction or building materials company.
* French or German.

**This Is Probably Not the Job for You If**

* You want to recommend and move on. Site 40 in year three is part of the job.
* You need a delivery organisation that hits every date. Ours is young, and you will be the one explaining a slip to the customer.
* You want a pure sales role. Landing new logos belongs to the Account Executives.

**What Success Looks Like**

* The first sites are past pilot, in contract and running, and the next batch is commercially ready before Delivery gets there.
* The customer's executive sponsor holds a written rollout plan with dates and KPIs, and treats it as theirs.
* Every site that went live did so on terms that make money for Hive.
* Hive has a documented way of running a global account, in use on the second one.

jobs.description:
## 🚀 About the role

ZOE is scaling rapidly. We’re broadening our product range, expanding across the EU, and beyond and entering major retail channels. As our manufacturing partner base, retailer requirements, and technical activity grow, we need dedicated internal ownership of our Quality Management System (QMS), product compliance, supplier controls, and quality processes.

As our **Quality & Technical Specialist**, you will be the guardian of trust in every product we launch. You’ll be the operational engine of our technical function—ensuring documentation is audit-ready, risks are visible, suppliers are governed, products are verified, and international launches have solid technical foundations.

## 👥 **About the team**

You’ll be joining our dynamic, fast-paced Operations team, reporting directly to the Food Supply Operations Manager. You will work closely with leads across inventory, procurement, and fulfillment within the broader supply chain team. In this role, you sit right at the centre of how ZOE creates, protects, and scales its products.

You will act as the key connector across internal teams and external partners. Internally, you will partner closely with Customer Experience to investigate product feedback, work with Legal and Regulatory to ensure compliance, and sync with Commercial and Marketing to enable seamless product launches. Externally, you will serve as the hands-on technical point of contact for our manufacturing partners, co-packers, independent testing laboratories, and supermarket retail technical teams. You will be the team’s operational expert on quality, with senior technical leadership always available to guide governance, long-term manufacturing strategy, and complex escalations.

## 🎯 What you’ll be doing

* **QMS & Compliance:** Maintain QMS records, audit schedules, and safety policies in line with BRCGS, HACCP, and UK/EU food regulations.

* **Product & Retail Specs:** Own finished product/packaging specifications, review artwork for labelling accuracy, and manage retailer technical portals.

* **Allergen Expertise:** Understanding of UK/EU allergen labelling laws and practical experience auditing allergen controls and cleaning validation at third-party manufacturing facilities.
* **Traceability or Recall Experience:** Hands-on experience conducting traceability audits and executing mock or live product recalls.
* **Data-Savvy & Adaptable:** Thrives analysing complaint trends and solving quality issues in a fast-paced scale-up.
* **Right to Work:** Permanent right to work in the UK or EU.
* **Willingness to Travel:** You are able and willing to travel to our manufacturing partners and supplier sites (primarily UK/EU) approximately once or twice every few months for routine audits, relationship building, and production trials.

## 👌🏼 The nice-to-haves

* Experience supporting physical product launches outside the UK (particularly EU or North America).
* Degree or formal apprenticeship in Food Science, Food Technology, or quality auditing.
* Experience navigating major retailer technical portals and due-diligence questionnaires.
* Curiosity and enthusiasm for using **AI tools and digital automation** to streamline operations and administrative work.

## ✨ What success looks like in this role

jobs.title: Performance Creative Editor
jobs.description:
## **🚀 About the Role**

We’re looking for a Performance Editor to join the creative engine behind ZOE’s paid social advertising.

This is an editing-first role. Around 80% of your time will be spent in Premiere and After Effects creating high-performing ads for Meta, TikTok, Google and other acquisition channels. Your primary focus will be growing Daily30 and the Gut Health Bar, creating performance creative that helps more people discover and purchase our physical products. While you’ll occasionally support campaigns for the ZOE App and Gut Health Test, your core focus will be building best-in-class creative for consumer products.

## **👥 About the Team**

You’ll join the Creative team, working day-to-day with User Acquisition managers, Creative Strategists, Designers, Copywriters and Creators. User Acquisition bring the commercial goals, creative strategy bring the performance insights, while you bring the creative execution, helping shape ideas and turning them into ads that perform. We move quickly, test constantly and care deeply about producing work that’s both creatively strong and commercially effective.

## **🎯 What You’ll Be Doing**

* **Edit performance creative every day**, transforming UGC, creator and brand footage into high-performing paid social ads for Daily30 and the Gut Health Bar across Meta, TikTok, Google and emerging platforms.
* **Create multiple creative variants**, testing different hooks, pacing, messaging, captions and CTAs to continually improve performance.
* **Bring products to life creatively**, showcasing ingredients, product experience, preparation, benefits and everyday moments in ways that make people stop scrolling and want to buy.
* **Bring ideas to the table**, contributing concepts, creative angles and improvements rather than simply executing briefs.
* **Apply strong creative judgement**, making thoughtful editing decisions that improve attention, engagement and conversion while balancing speed with quality.
* **Use performance data to improve your work**, learning from results and applying those insights to future edits.
* **Build scalable editing workflows**, using templates, AI-assisted tools and repeatable processes to increase output without compromising creative quality.
* **Own your projects from brief to delivery**, collaborating closely with User Acquisition, copywriters and designers to produce work that delivers measurable business impact.
* **Jump behind the camera when needed**, capturing quick pieces of content, new hooks, product demonstrations or social-first moments that strengthen the creative. We value people who are resourceful, scrappy and willing to make ideas happen, not just edit what’s already been shot.

## **🧠 What You’ll Bring**

**Experience & Craft**

* A strong portfolio demonstrating paid social video editing, with multiple creative variants and clear evidence of performance thinking. **This is essential.**
* Experience creating conversion-focused creative for DTC, SaaS or consumer brands.
* Recent experience delivering performance video campaigns across **Meta, TikTok and Google**, with a strong understanding of platform-specific creative best practices.
* Advanced skills in **Premiere Pro, After Effects, Photoshop, Figma and CapCut**, with the confidence to choose the right tool for the job.
* Strong experience creating paid social video, motion graphics, AI-assisted creative, voiceovers and end-to-end asset production.
* The confidence to independently make creative decisions that elevate the work, rather than simply following a brief.

**Thinking & Mindset**

* You’re an editor first. Your favourite part of the job is being in the timeline making creative work better.
* **You have excellent creative judgement.** You understand that the goal isn’t to make the most polished advert possible, it’s to make the most effective one. You’re comfortable dialling the fidelity of the work up or down depending on the creative opportunity, always protecting the reputation of the ZOE brand while helping us improve the health of millions through creative that performs.
* You’re naturally curious about why ads succeed or fail and enjoy using performance data to improve your creative decisions.
* You have a bias for action. If the creative needs a new hook, another shot or a better ending, you don’t wait for someone else to solve it. You’re happy to pick up a camera, record a voiceover, experiment with AI or try three different edits until you find what works.

## 🌱 About ZOE

ZOE is a gut health science company. We turn world-leading nutrition research into everyday products that help people feel healthier, including the ZOE app, our at-home Gut Health Test, Daily30+ and the Gut Health Bar. Our scientists run the largest nutrition study in the world, and the ZOE Science & Nutrition podcast is one of the most listened-to health podcasts in the UK. Our mission is to transform the health of millions by giving them the most advanced science and technology.

## 👥 About the Team

Our [Engineering team](https://joinzoe.notion.site/Shape-the-future-of-health-313f5c8e549681a5b26ae626e0875539) sits at the heart of that mission. We're a distributed team of around 40 people across the UK and EU, and we like solving complex problems together. We bring a wide mix of skills, from front-end, back-end, full-stack and mobile engineering to machine learning, data science and analytics, to build the experiences that guide our members through their health journey.

We're proud of the diversity in our team: 39% female and 61% male, with colleagues from many backgrounds, cultures and lived experiences. We believe this makes us stronger, more creative and better able to serve our global community.

Collaboration is core to how we work. Engineers at ZOE partner closely with data scientists, analysts, product managers and product designers to bring new ideas to life. Depending on the project, we also work with marketing, finance, legal and other teams, so the work is highly cross-functional and impactful.

Above all, we value curiosity, openness and empowerment. We encourage everyone to share ideas, keep learning and shape how we work, whether that's experimenting with new technology, improving our ways of working or finding better ways to support our members.

## 🚀 About the role

We're looking for a Full Stack Engineer with a front-end focus to help us build world-class digital experiences. ZOE runs a full-stack environment, but this role is for someone who loves crafting seamless, performant, responsive and beautiful user interfaces.

Your main focus will be [**zoe.com**](http://zoe.com), the place where people discover ZOE, learn about our science and join as members or buy our products. Your work will directly shape how millions of people first experience ZOE, and you'll see its impact in the data.

You'll spend most of your time in TypeScript, React and Next.js. You'll also work in our backend services (Kotlin or Python) to make sure the data you need is available, well structured and delivered efficiently. You'll help shape and grow our web design system with design and engineering, and you'll launch A/B tests and work with analysts to understand the results.

* **Design partnership:** working closely with UX designers to turn high-fidelity designs into fluid, accessible and performant components.
* **Design system:** contributing to and helping grow our shared component library and web design system.
* **Experimentation:** launching A/B tests and working with analysts to interpret results and improve the user journey.
* **Bridging the stack:** collaborating on API design and implementing backend changes where new front-end features need them.
* **Engineering excellence:** writing clean, testable, maintainable code and shipping to production regularly, ideally daily.
* **Growth:** learning from and working alongside senior engineers, sharing knowledge with others, and growing into a technical owner of parts of our web platform.

* Have **working knowledge of a backend language** (such as Python, Kotlin or Java) and feel comfortable navigating an API or database schema.

## ✨ Nice to have

jobs.title: Director of Biostatistics
jobs.description:
**🍊Our mission**

Great science regularly stalls in the clinic, not because the science is wrong, but because the company behind it lacks the capital, infrastructure, or focus to take it all the way through. Today’s clinical-stage biopharma model is broken, and as a result promising treatments never reach patients.

Our mission is to fix this: we’re building the next generation of biopharma by in-licensing clinical-stage therapeutic assets and developing them through Lindus Health’s integrated, technology-first clinical trial infrastructure. We’re a new initiative, but we’re building on a proven foundation - the same infrastructure that has delivered 82% of Lindus Health’s sponsor trials on or ahead of timeline, across 40+ completed trials across the US and Europe.

We’re in-licensing 5-7 clinical-stage, typically Phase-2-ready assets, funded directly from Lindus Health’s balance sheet. We’re targeting deal close on our first assets through 2026, with first trials launching in H1 2027.

**🍊 About the role**

As Lindus Therapeutics builds out its portfolio through in-licensing, the Director of Biostatistics owns statistical strategy across that portfolio and stays hands-on, personally leading the statistics on live programmes from protocol through clinical study report. It's a genuine coach-player role - as much applied biostatistician as director.

This seat carries real weight: the statistical rigour of an incoming asset's data package shapes deal terms and development risk, and it's Lindus Therapeutics' primary statistical voice with regulators. You'll work closely with clinical, medical, data architecture, and business development colleagues, and build out the wider biostatistics function as the portfolio grows.

**🍊 About you**

**We'd like to hear from you if…**

* PhD in statistics or biostatistics with 10+ years' relevant pharma/biotech experience, or MS with 15+ years, including lead statistician experience across multiple Phase I/II programmes (Phase III and CSR experience a plus)
* Personally interacted with health authorities on at least one programme, ideally an early-phase IND (NDA also acceptable), including formal meetings or written correspondence; FDA preferred, EMA also considered. Adaptive trial design experience required
* Experience setting statistical strategy at a programme or portfolio level, with strong knowledge of CDISC standards, regulatory submission requirements, and current drug development trends
* Excellent programming skills, including independently generating analysis output; R and/or SAS fluency preferred, and familiarity with applying AI/ML tools to statistical workflows a plus
* Experience evaluating external clinical data through due diligence, licensing, or M&A activity is a plus
* Comfortable operating as both a leader and a hands-on contributor, with excellent written and verbal communication skills across technical and non-technical audiences

**🍊 What you'll focus on**

* **Statistical strategy & functional leadership:** Set statistical strategy across the portfolio as it grows, and lead the biostatistics, statistical programming, and medical writing functions - priorities, ways of working, hiring, and SOPs.
* **Lead statistician on active programmes:** Personally lead the statistics on active and incoming programmes, from protocol development through database lock and clinical study report - authoring and reviewing SAPs, sample size and power calculations, and randomisation schemes, and reviewing output at key milestones including interim analyses and DSMB packages.
* **Regulatory representation:** Serve as the primary statistical voice with regulators - meetings, briefing documents, and responses to health authority queries - and author and review the statistical sections of regulatory submissions, including IND and NDA filings.
* **Due diligence & asset evaluation:** Assess the statistical rigour of clinical data packages for assets under consideration for in-licensing - trial design quality, endpoint selection, strength of signal - and flag statistical risk that could affect development strategy or deal terms.
* **Delivery oversight & innovation:** Oversee statistical programming deliverables (analysis datasets, tables, listings, figures, consistent with CDISC standards) and medical writing output for CSRs and submissions, evaluate external CRO/FSP partnerships where needed, and identify where AI and machine learning tools can meaningfully improve statistical workflows.

## 

**🍊What we offer (UK)**

Make an impact across all areas of our business and fix one of the world's most broken industries.

* **Competitive salary**, plus meaningful **stock options**
* **Flexible working:** We have an incredible office near London Bridge and encourage people to work **3 days per week from the office**
* **30 days annual leave in addition to Bank Holidays**
* **£60 monthly wellness allowance,** which you can spend on our company health insurance scheme through AXA, a wellhub membership, or wellness activities and expenses of your choice!
* **Enhanced Parental Leave:** 16 weeks full pay for **primary caregiver** and 6 weeks full pay for **secondary caregiver**
* **£1,000 Learning and Development allowance** each year to put towards courses, certifications, and development
* **Regular whole company and team events**, both in person and virtually
* **Access to gym and retail discounts** through our benefits platform **Happl**
* **A well-stocked pantry and drinks fridge**, Monday breakfast spread and catered team lunch on a Thursday for the UK office every week!
* **Cycle-to-work scheme** and other salary sacrifice options available
* **Charity events and fundraising opportunities** through our charity partnership with the **Forward Trust**

## **🍊 Our hiring process**

* Initial conversation with our Senior Talent Partner, Cam (30 minutes)
* Second conversation with the VP of Data (30 minutes)
* Technical interview with Biostatistics experts (60 minutes)
* Values interview with 2 Senior Leadership Team members (30 minutes)

**We will only contact you from** [**lindushealth.com**](http://lindushealth.com) **email addresses. Please check the spelling of emails which appear to come from Lindus carefully before responding. We will never ask for your financial information over email.**

jobs.title: Agentic Compiler Engineer
jobs.description:
## ABOUT KOG

Kog builds a co-designed inference stack for real-time AI agents on standard datacenter GPUs, spanning model architecture, inference engine, compilers, and low-level GPU kernels.

On the model side, we developed Laneformer 2B and Delayed Tensor Parallelism (DTP), a Transformer architecture that overlaps communication with useful computation and weight streaming.

On the systems side, the Kog Inference Engine runs this stack on standard AMD and NVIDIA datacenter GPUs.

Kog generates 3,500 tokens/s per request on 8 AMD MI300X GPUs and 2,100 tokens/s per request on 8 NVIDIA H200 GPUs, in FP16 at batch size 1, with quantization and speculative decoding disabled.

Our next major project is AGCO, our agentic compiler. AGCO is designed to optimize LLMs across different GPUs and optimization targets, including very fast inference.

The team has 10 people, including 9 engineers and researchers and 4 PhDs.

Test it at playground.kog.ai. Read the technical details on the Kog Labs blog.

## WHAT YOU WILL WORK ON

You will work directly on AGCO.

The goal is to build a system that can explore ways to optimize LLM execution, generate changes, compile them, check correctness, run them on real hardware, measure the results, and use this feedback to guide the next optimization.

You will contribute to areas such as:

* Compiler and IR design for representing and transforming LLM computations.
* Optimization passes, lowering, and code generation.
* Search methods for exploring different implementations and execution strategies.
* Verification and correctness checks for generated changes.
* GPU execution, profiling, and performance optimization.
* LLM inference across operators, memory, parallelism, and communication.
* Optimization loops that connect generated changes to measurements on real GPUs.

One direction we are exploring combines an IR, a verifier, a compiler, and a search optimizer. We plan to start with focused problems, build working prototypes, and extend the system from what we learn.

Your main area will depend on your experience, skills, and interests. You may focus more on compilers, GPU systems, or LLM inference while working closely with people across the full stack.

## WHAT WE LOOK FOR

We look for engineers with deep technical expertise and original work in at least one area relevant to AGCO.

Relevant experience includes:

* Compiler engineering, including optimization passes, IRs, lowering, code generation, LLVM, or MLIR.
* GPU programming with CUDA, HIP, Metal, Vulkan, or similar technologies.
* GPU performance work involving kernels, memory, synchronization, profiling, or hardware behavior.
* LLM inference engines and performance optimization.
* Attention, MoE, parallelism, communication, or other systems-level parts of LLM execution.
* Formal verification, equivalence checking, SAT/SMT, or related methods.
* Systems that generate, search, test, benchmark, or optimize code automatically.

We care about what you personally built and the technical decisions behind it. Strong candidates can explain the problem, their approach, the alternatives they explored, and how they measured the result.

We review technical work during the process. This can be public code, an upstream contribution, a paper, a thesis, a technical project, or a detailed write-up based on work you can share.

## WHAT WE OFFER

You will join a small team building AGCO as a core part of Kog's technology.

* Work at the intersection of compilers, GPU systems, and LLM inference.
* Direct access to engineers working across the full inference stack.
* A fast loop from an optimization idea to compilation, execution, verification, and measurement on real GPUs.
* The opportunity to go deep in your strongest technical area while expanding into the other parts of the stack.
* High ownership over technical decisions and systems that will shape how Kog optimizes LLM inference.

This role is based in Paris, and we are looking for candidates who can relocate to Paris and work closely with the team.

jobs.title: Responsable bourses et mobilité internationale F/H
jobs.description:
#### Vos missions

Vous assurez la gestion des dispositifs de financement de la mobilité internationale des étudiants et des personnels et contribuez au pilotage de celui-ci.

Vous garantissez la qualité, la conformité et le suivi administratif et financier des dispositifs de bourses, notamment dans le cadre du programme Erasmus+.

En complément de cette mission principale, vous contribuez à la mise en œuvre des engagements de l’UTC dans le cadre de la Charte Erasmus+ et de ses grandes priorités, inclusion et diversité, transition écologique, transformation numérique, participation à la vie démocratique et aux valeurs européennes.

Dans ce cadre, vous participez au développement d’actions à destination des étudiants et des personnels : événements, actions de sensibilisation, formations courtes, ressources et formations en ligne.

En tant que référent-e « Transition numérique » Erasmus+ de la DRI, vous accompagnez également la transformation numérique des processus de mobilité et participez activement au déploiement, au paramétrage fonctionnel et à l’appropriation du logiciel de gestion de la mobilité internationale et des partenariats universitaires au sein de la DRI.

#### Vos activités

**1. Coordonner l’activité du pôle « Bourses »**

* Assurer la gestion des différents dispositifs de financement de la mobilité internationale des étudiants et des personnels

* Coordonner la gestion des bourses Erasmus+ et des autres dispositifs de financement nationaux, régionaux ou institutionnels

* Organiser et promouvoir les bourses de mobilités internationales (campagnes d’attribution des aides, information et accompagnement des étudiants et personnels)

* Assurer le suivi administratif et financier des dossiers de bourses de mobilité internationale et budgets dédiés

* Produire les données, indicateurs, bilans et statistiques

* Garantir le respect des critères d’éligibilité, des procédures et des règles propres aux différents programmes

* Participer à la définition et à l’évolution des critères et procédures, dans une logique de simplification, de fiabilisation et d’amélioration continue.

* Contribuer aux rapports Erasmus+, aux bilans institutionnels ainsi qu’aux contrôles et audits éventuels

* Assurer une veille sur l’évolution des dispositifs de financement de la mobilité internationale

**2. Accompagner le déploiement de la solution numérique dédiée à la gestion de la mobilité internationale et la transformation numérique des processus**

Dans le cadre du déploiement de cet outil à l’UTC, vous participez à la transformation et à la dématérialisation des processus de gestion de la mobilité internationale.

À ce titre, vous contribuez notamment au/à l’:

* Déploiement de la solution numérique : analyse des processus existants, workflows, tests, paramétrage…

* Amélioration régulière : cohérence, fiabilité des données, évolution

* Accompagnement des membres du service : prise en main, tutoriels

* Accompagnement des étudiants et personnels

* Développement d’une utilisation experte progressive : indicateurs et suivi…

Vous participez ainsi à faire de la solution numérique un outil d’amélioration et de transformation des processus.

**3. Contribuer à la mise en œuvre des priorités de la Charte Erasmus+**

Contribuer à la déclinaison opérationnelle des engagements de l’UTC dans le cadre de la Charte Erasmus+ et de ses quatre grandes priorités :

* Inclusion et diversité : favoriser l’accès à la mobilité des publics ayant moins d’opportunités et améliorer leur accompagnement.

* Transition écologique : promouvoir une mobilité internationale plus responsable et sensibiliser aux enjeux environnementaux.

* Transformation numérique : développer les usages et ressources numériques liés à la mobilité et accompagner la dématérialisation des dispositifs Erasmus+.

* Participation et citoyenneté européenne : développer des actions favorisant la connaissance de l’Europe, de ses valeurs et des opportunités offertes par Erasmus+.

**4. Contribuer à la promotion des actions et événements à destination des étudiants**

Contribuer à la promotion de la mobilité internationale et des priorités Erasmus+ :

* événements étudiants (Erasmus Days, rencontres interculturelles, témoignages, challenges, etc.) ;

* ateliers de préparation au départ et de valorisation du retour de mobilité ;

* actions autour de l’Europe, de l’inclusion, de l’interculturalité et de la mobilité durable.

**5. Contribuer au développement des formations courtes et des ressources pédagogiques**

Contribuer à la conception et à l’animation de formations courtes, ateliers et ressources pédagogiques, en présentiel, en ligne ou en format hybride, dans le contexte de la mission (tutoriels et ressources numériques destinés aux étudiants et personnels).

**6. Participer aux projets transversaux de la DRI**

Participer, selon les besoins, aux projets transversaux de la Direction aux Relations Internationales : projets Erasmus+, alliance européenne SUNRISE, événements internationaux, actions de promotion de la mobilité, internationalisation des formations et démarches d’amélioration continue

Travailler en interaction avec les autres pôles de la DRI, les services et enseignants de l’UTC, les associations étudiantes et les partenaires institutionnels.

#### Informations complémentaires

**Dates pour candidater**

Du 29/09/2026 au 29/10/2026

**Type de recrutement et date prévisionnelle de recrutement**

Poste ouvert aux personnels de catégorie A assistant ingénieur, par voie statutaire (mutation, détachement) ou contractuelle (contrat à durée déterminée d’un an, prolongation possible pouvant aboutir à un CDI) – pourvoi immédiat

**Salaire mensuel brut**

Suivant statut ou par la voie contractuelle, selon expérience

Pour les fonctionnaires, RIFSEEP : ASI - Groupe 1

Pour les agents contractuels, salaire mensuel brut de 1 867 euros à 3 111 euros, selon expérience

**Volume horaire**

37 heures et 30 minutes/semaine - 1 607 heures/an

**Congés**

50 jours de congés, RTT comprise, par année universitaire

**Environnement et contexte de travail**

Vous intégrerez la direction aux relations internationales et serez placé(e) sous la responsabilité hiérarchique de la directrice aux relations internationales.

Des déplacements occasionnels (formations, réunions, évènements) sont à prévoir.

**Contexte**

L’ouverture à l’international constitue un pilier du modèle pédagogique de l’UTC et ce depuis sa création. Elle se traduit par une stratégie internationale ambitieuse, des projets d’envergure comme des campus à l’international et une alliance des universités européennes et d’autres projets et partenariats structurants. L’UTC a aujourd’hui plus de 220 partenaires internationaux dans le monde. Certains de ces partenariats ont plus de 40 ans d’existence. L’UTC continue à consolider un réseau européen solide et vise à être un acteur clé dans l’évolution du modèle de l’enseignement supérieur européen.

Dans ce cadre, l’établissement vise une mobilité internationale sortante de 100% des étudiants de l’UTC. La mobilité Erasmus+ s’envisage dans ce contexte de la promotion de la mobilité, à la gestion des bourses associés jusqu’aux retours de la mobilité.

Pour renforcer cette mobilité, nous accompagnons les étudiantes et étudiants de l’UTC dans l’ensemble des démarches y compris l’obtention des bourses de mobilité internationale.

Finalement, la direction aux relations internationales vise également à promouvoir l’interculturalité, renforcer l’inclusion, la digitalisation et la transition environnementale et ce dans le respect des priorités de la charte Erasmus+ et celles de la stratégie de l’UTC.

La personne recrutée pourrait contribuer à proposer et développer des actions pour l’implémentation des priorités de la charte Erasmus+ à l’UTC.

**Diplôme et formation**

Diplôme :Bac + 2 au minimum, DUT ou licence apprécié(e)

Domaine de formation : Gestion administrative, relations internationales, langues étrangères appliquées....

jobs.title: FPGA Engineer - Electronic Warfare
jobs.description:
### About Alta Ares

Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.

Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Founded in 2024, we have grown to 90 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.

## Role & Mission

* Own the development of FPGA functions for our electronic warfare and signals intelligence capabilities, from initial architecture to validation on operational hardware.
* Work with systems and algorithm engineers to define processing requirements and assess implementation feasibility.
* Build RTL modules in VHDL or SystemVerilog to process digitized RF signals, extract relevant information, and generate waveforms.
* Adapt and validate DSP algorithms for FPGA implementation, balancing numerical accuracy, processing speed, and hardware resources.
* Integrate acquisition and processing chains, including digital down-conversion, filtering, channelization, FFT, detection, direction-finding, and classification.
* Establish verification methods and testbenches to check functional behavior and performance throughout development.
* Connect programmable logic to RF converters and embedded processors, defining data transfers, control interfaces, clocking, and synchronization.
* Resolve implementation constraints, achieve timing closure, and optimize resource utilization and power consumption.
* Bring up FPGA designs on target boards, investigate integration issues, and correlate measured behavior with simulation results.
* Contribute to laboratory and field testing alongside RF, software, and systems engineers.
* Maintain clear design records, interface specifications, and validation evidence.
* Improve reusable FPGA components and development practices as the product portfolio grows.

# Candidate Profile

* MSc in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Signal Processing, or a related field.
* Strong experience developing and verifying RTL in VHDL or SystemVerilog, with a focus on digital signal processing.
* Practical experience implementing designs on SoC FPGAs, including synthesis, implementation, timing analysis, and hardware debugging.
* Strong understanding of sampled signals, frequency conversion, digital filtering, spectral analysis, and fixed-point numerical behavior.
* Ability to reason across FPGA, processor, and RF hardware boundaries when making design decisions.
* Experience modelling algorithms and comparing reference models with hardware results; familiarity with MATLAB, Simulink, Python, or HLS is a plus.
* Familiarity with RF measurements and laboratory equipment, including spectrum analyzers, signal generators, and oscilloscopes, is a plus.
* Prior experience in electronic warfare is welcome but not required.

## Skills & Qualities

* Hands-on engineer who enjoys taking designs from simulation to working hardware.
* Methodical approach to debugging, with the ability to isolate problems across complex signal chains.
* Able to own a technical scope independently and communicate progress, risks, and trade-offs clearly.
* Rigorous approach to verification, documentation, and design traceability.
* Comfortable collaborating across disciplines and adapting to evolving product requirements.
* Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to operate autonomously in a fast-growing company.
* High integrity and professionalism in handling sensitive defense technologies.

If you are energetic, curious, motivated and ambitious, be part of our world. Apply now and define the future of work!

## The position

This is an exciting time to join Remote and make a personal difference in the global employment space in Employee Lifecycle Operations, by joining our Employee Lifecycle team.

As a Senior Lifecycle Specialist (OHS), you will ensure that all activities related to the occupational health and safety of employees are performed effectively, compliantly, and on time across multiple countries supported by Remote. You will be responsible for identifying, engaging, and managing vendor partnerships, driving contract management processes, and be in charge of rolling out all events related to health and safety across the globe for Remote’s employees.

You will be reporting to Employee Lifecycle Manager.

## Requirements

* Significant work experience in a digital environment
* BA/BS degree or equivalent.
* Progressive management plus required examiner experience within Workers’ Compensation insurance industry.
* Experience scouting, onboarding, and/or managing insurance partners and brokers
* Ability to quickly engage and support external employees and vendors across multiple countries
* Good analytical skills, ability to map processes

* A growth and problem-solving mindset. You can shift tasks and priorities when circumstances change and do so quickly and effectively

**Risk Financing:**

**Data Analysis and Reporting:**

**Stakeholder Engagement:**

**Customer Support:**

* Provide prospects, customers and their employees with the necessary support on Workers Compensation insurance coverage, exclusions and overall risk management advise

* Collaborate closely with the Occupational Health and Safety team, brokers, and insurers to support the claim management process for both internal and external employees

## Practicals

* **You'll report to:** Senior Manager, Contract management, Lifecycle
* **Team:** Lifecycle Operations

## Application process

2. Interview with future manager
3. Team Interview
4. Executive Interview

We hope to inspire other companies to support global talent-hiring and bring local wealth to developing countries.

## **About Mistral**
